Jan Selzer works in the noise unit of the Institute for Occupational Safety and Health of the German Social Accident Insurance (IFA) and has been a doctoral candidate in technical acoustics at TU Berlin since November 2020. Like many acousticians, he came to the field through music, playing in bands and co-founding a sound engineering club at school, then studied media technology at what was then Fachhochschule Düsseldorf. An internship at the broadcaster WDR followed, then a bachelor’s thesis at Ford in vehicle NVH, building a test rig to measure how materials reduce impulsiveness.

That sparked his interest in auditory perception. As a research assistant at Düsseldorf’s Institute of Sound and Vibration Engineering (ISAVE), he ran listening tests, taught and wrote a master’s thesis modeling the salient hearing of environmental sounds; Professor Jörg Becker-Schweitzer encouraged him toward a doctorate. At the IFA, the doctorate is not a job requirement, but part of his working time can go to it.

His working title is “Instrumental assessment of auditory load at work.” He tests work tasks under different acoustic conditions in a listening booth at the institute in Sankt Augustin and runs headphone experiments in offices, probing the non-auditory effects of noise. The thesis will be a monograph with no publication requirement, though he has presented at DAGA 2022 in Stuttgart and Inter-Noise 2022 in Glasgow. He also advises on noise reduction, measures noise in open-plan offices and workplaces with hazardous noise levels, and sits on standards committees. Professor André Fiebig supervises the doctorate.

Adapted into Chinese by Fanyu Meng from Jan Selzer’s first-person profile in Akustik Journal, published by the German Acoustical Society (DEGA).
